first.rationale:
The two acute, measurable declines are activation (-6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (-4% QoQ). Onboarding shortening (memory_86) sits directly on the declining metric and, per memory_31, upstream signup simplification also lifts first-week activation, so a single onboarding/signup-friction experiment plausibly addresses both declines at once. Activation messaging (memory_91) is the close second but treats the symptom later in the funnel; if friction is the cause, fixing entry beats nudging survivors. Promotional pricing is the tempting reflex given the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 explicitly records materially worse 30-day retention and warns against generalizing it — that directly contradicts the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I decline it despite the competitive pressure. Referral incentives (memory_57) are safe but act on established customers and do nothing for the two metrics that are actually falling. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is a different segment from the observed decline.

I spend both verification pulls on the memories my chosen action rests on rather than on the ones I am rejecting: memory_86 and memory_31 are load-bearing, and I need their original records to check (a) effect size and whether the 'durable' lift was measured past week one, (b) whether the baseline populations resemble today's traffic mix, and (c) whether the earlier gains were already banked, in which case current declines have a different cause and re-cutting friction will not recover them. Verifying memory_73 would only confirm a decision I have already made against.

Downstream value risk: memory_31's mechanism is cutting required signup fields, and memory_44 says enterprise prospects convert best through sales-assisted flows, which depend on qualification data captured at entry. Stripping fields to lift SMB activation can quietly degrade lead routing and enterprise pipeline quality — a cost that shows up in qualified revenue, not in the activation dashboard. The experiment must therefore segment self-serve from enterprise-intent traffic, preserve qualification capture on the latter, and instrument pipeline quality as a guardrail alongside activation.

Uncertainty preserved: these are consolidated summaries without effect sizes or confidence intervals, the QoQ declines may share an unmeasured common cause (traffic-mix shift, seasonality, or competitor siphoning the most motivated SMB signups), and correlational inheritance is not causal proof. Standard experiment with holdout and guardrail metrics rather than broad rollout; if verification shows the original lifts were small, short-lived, or already realized, I would fall back to activation_messaging.
